messages:
Alex: Heads-up — customer feedback from FinCo: they have multiple tool integrations and need a clear compatibility story for function/tool calling. Proposing a short "interop guidelines" doc + minimal protocol for version negotiation. Thoughts?

Priya: Strong +1. We need two things: 1) backward compatibility guarantees for v1 -> v2 and 2) explicit migration path for customers. Can you sketch the guarantees we want?

Alex: Sketch: (a) Add a lightweight header `X-Invoke-Version` with semver-ish string (major only for breaking), (b) runtime supports `strict` and `permissive` parsing modes, default `permissive`, (c) servers emit deprecation telemetry when they receive older major versions.

Jonah: Agree on header. Implementation note: we should avoid extra RTTs for negotiation. Header-only negotiation is simplest. For parsing modes: default permissive means unknown fields ignored; strict will return 4xx with error code `invoke.schema_mismatch`.

Sam: Operationally we need telemetry fields tied to every call so we can measure adoption and parsing errors. Minimal telemetry: `invoke.protocol_version`, `tool_id`, `tool_schema_version`, `result_shape`, `parse_error` (bool), `latency_ms`. Add `canary_flag` for rollout.

Marta: SDKs will need to surface the header and map package versions -> `tool_schema_version`. Also we should document the recommended error shape so SDKs can auto-retry with fallback shapes.

Priya: Launch gating idea: require docs + SDK support for JS/Python + automated e2e against 3 representative customers + telemetry showing parse_error <= 1% in the canary cohort for 48h. If any signals fail, rollback to previous default behavior.

Jonah: Implementation timeline ask: eng-platform team can do metadata header + permissive parsing in 2 sprints, strict mode + error codes + telemetry in 1 more. Need product to prioritize canary customers and create test vectors.

Alex: For schema evolution rules propose: - non-breaking additions allowed (new optional fields) - renaming/removal => new major - tightening types (string -> int) => new major. Keep it explicit in doc with examples.

Priya: Customer ask: FinCo wants automatic fallback to a JSON `result` string if the structured result fails parsing. That seems like a permissive-mode behavior we can standardize: `fallback_result` field that servers fill when they serialize raw output. Doable?

Jonah: `fallback_result` is doable but we should limit size and warn about privacy/PII if we persist raw text. Add KMS/retention notes to doc.

Sam: Ops: rollout plan: 1) internal beta 2) opt-in canary via header `X-Invoke-Optin: canary` for customers 3) monitored ramp by traffic. Gate: <1% parse_error and latency delta <5% for 72h.

Marta: Docs needed: migration checklist, sample SDK snippets, tests for permissive vs strict, and a mini spec table showing allowed changes per semver. I'll draft and send PR to docs repo.

Alex: Action items: Jonah + Sam to create RFC PR for header + telemetry (due EOD Fri), Marta to start docs PR, Priya to coordinate FinCo canary and assemble test vectors. I'll schedule 30m decision sync on Tuesday. @everyone please react with :thumbsup: if ok.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued for branch "invoke-interop/prototype" — build started.

Priya: TL;DR: We aim for header negotiation + permissive default + strict opt-in + telemetry + documented migration + canary gating. Prioritize this as P1 for next quarter if we get two enterprise canaries.

Alex: Thanks — will formalize spec and share pre-read before Tuesday sync."
